package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions used in Barracuda ESG prior to patch for CVE-2023-7102)
package_info.why_malicious: The package was leveraged as part of a supply chain attack due to a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2023-7102) that allowed arbitrary code execution when parsing specially crafted Excel files. While the package itself is not inherently malicious, its exploitation enabled attackers to execute malicious payloads on Barracuda ESG appliances.

execution_context.file_location: Spreadsheet::ParseExcel library (invoked by Amavis virus scanner within Barracuda ESG)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker-supplied, specially crafted Excel file triggers arbitrary code execution via a vulnerability in Spreadsheet::ParseExcel.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During runtime, when the Amavis scanner processes an email with a malicious Excel attachment, the crafted file exploits a vulnerability in Spreadsheet::ParseExcel, leading to arbitrary code execution on the ESG appliance.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code path allows untrusted input (Excel file) to trigger code execution, which is a classic exploitation vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects the library to safely parse Excel files without executing code; instead, it allows attacker-controlled input to execute arbitrary commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be parsing Excel files for data extraction or malware scanning, not code execution.
key_indicators: Parsing untrusted files leads to code execution
Used in a high-value security appliance context

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted Excel file as an email attachment to a target organization using Barracuda ESG.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious file is scanned by Amavis, invoking Spreadsheet::ParseExcel.

attack_chain.action: Amavis virus scanner processes the attachment, calling Spreadsheet::ParseExcel to parse the Excel file.
Exploit in Spreadsheet::ParseExcel allows arbitrary code execution on the Barracuda ESG appliance.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains code execution, enabling further compromise or malware deployment.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected process spawning or command execution during Excel file parsing
Unusual network connections initiated by the ESG appliance after email scanning
Crash or instability in Amavis or Spreadsheet::ParseExcel when handling Excel attachments
file_indicators: Excel files with malformed or non-standard structures targeting Spreadsheet::ParseExcel
Unusual temporary files or scripts created during email scanning
network_indicators: Outbound connections from ESG appliances to attacker-controlled infrastructure following email scanning
C2 traffic patterns originating from ESG appliances
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for abnormal process activity or command execution on Barracuda ESG appliances during or immediately after email attachment scanning, especially involving Excel files. Inspect logs for errors or crashes in Amavis or Spreadsheet::ParseExcel. Analyze incoming Excel attachments for exploit attempts targeting CVE-2023-7102. Correlate with unexpected outbound network connections from ESG devices.
